Criminal Appeal No. 10785 of 2024

 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Ashish Sinha - Advocate for the appellant.
 Ms. Seema Jaiswal - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/St
 Shri Bhasker Pandey - Advocate for the objector.

Order 
This criminal appeal has been filed under Section 14-A(1 & 2) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989.

2. Appellant Manish Patel has been arrested in connection with Crime No.818 of 2024 registered at Police Station Gadarwara, District- Narsinghpur for the offences punishable under Sections 363,
376, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and Section 3(1)(W)(i), 3(2)(va) and 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
Appellant is in jail since 31.07.2024.

3. Prosecution story in brief is that in January 2021, May 2023 and on 19.06.2024, appellant established physical relation with prosecutrix aged 23 years without her consent and against her will.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that prosecutrix and appellant were known to each other/were acquainted with each other since NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50781 2 CRA-10785-2024 last seven years.
Prosecutrix intended to marry with appellant and she does not intend to marry with anyone else.
Appellant did not establish physical relation with prosecutrix.

There is no evidence pertaining to engagement of prosecutrix with someone else and that above Manish Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61757256/
1 relationship got broke down and on account of the same, prosecutrix consumed poison and was admitted in Hospital.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also urged that after completion of Investigation, charge- sheet has been filed.
There are no CDRs and whatsApp chatt on record.
Mobile of prosecutrix has not been recovered.
Appellant's mobile has not been sent for Cyber Forensic Examination.

On above grounds,
it is urged that appellant be released on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the objector submits that from evidence on record, it is clearly established that appellant established physical relation with prosecutrix against her will and thereafter prosecutrix consumed poison on account of blackmailing by the appellant.
There are documents/evidence pertaining to prosecutrix admission in Hospital and with respect to her engagement.
On above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
6. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
7. Looking to the evidence available on record, especially, pertaining to blackmailing etc. by appellant, I deem it proper to release appellant on bail.
Consequently, this appeal stands allowed.

8. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50781 3 CRA-10785-2024 with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
10. Certified copy as per rules.
